messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: page fired: GPU_MEMORY_PRESSURE on pool-g1 (region-us-west-2) - 12% of GPUs above mem-threshold; auto-shedder started. Pager: PagerDuty incident #PD-8472

pagerduty: Incoming alert from metric: gpu.mem.used_ratio > 0.92 for > 2m - page generated to rotation: sam_w -> tara_ops -> cheng_l

sam_w: acked - I'm awake, grabbing logs and pool status

sam_w: quick check: `rsvc pool describe pool-g1 --region us-west-2` shows 8 nodes, 2 in degrade, 1 under eviction

sam_w: pulling recent container logs from node gpu-11: `kubectl -n redwood logs -l node=gpu-11 --tail=200`

sam_w: snippet from logs (cuda errors):
```
E 03:12:05 cuda:cuMemAlloc failed: out of memory
W 03:12:05 kvcache: eviction loop triggered, evicted 243 entries
E 03:12:06 runtime: failed to allocate workspace: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED
```

tara_ops: seeing repeated KV cache churn in metrics + slightly elevated latency on hosted endpoints (latency p95 up 80ms). Which models on pool-g1?

cheng_l: pool-g1 serving gpt-neo-16k-v3 (quantized q8) and a few smaller LMs. Recent deploy?

sam_w: no deploys in the last 45m. Looks like a sudden increase in KV cache retention due to several long-context requests. Could be a bot or regression in users.

marta_cs: product is flagging a couple customers reporting 503s for generation requests in us-west-2, one on premium tier. Need impact summary for them.

sam_w: mitigation plan: 1) throttle new long-context requests at the edge for pool-g1 via temporary route override, 2) bounce the most memory-hungry replica jobs, 3) add short-term scale-up + move canaries to other pools. Starting step 1 now.

sam_w: applying override: `redwood route update --pool pool-g1 --max-context 8192 --priority 50 --reason "emergency mem pressure"`

oncall-bot: Route override applied by sam_w. :white_check_mark:

cheng_l: running `rsvc node drain gpu-11` to free memory for immediate reclaim. If we can free one node, eviction should calm down.

sam_w: monitoring kvcache evictions and node-level free memory. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/gpu/mem/pool-g1 (link)

tara_ops: noticed a burst of requests from ip-range 54.120.0.0/16 hitting long-context endpoint. Could be a customer test or a bad CI job. Can someone add a temporary rate limit on that CIDR?

sam_w: adding IP rate limit rule in the edge WAF now. `edgectl ratelimit add --cidr 54.120.0.0/16 --rate 50r/m --reason "mitigate mem pressure"`

marta_cs: pinging affected customer owners, creating a brief incident outreach note: "We're investigating memory pressure in us-west-2 affecting generation requests; mitigation underway, might see transient 503s. ETA next update in 20m."

sam_w: node drain finished on gpu-11, freed ~90% GPU mem. kvcache eviction rate dropped by 70%. Latency trending down.

cheng_l: while freeing, found one long-running batch job with very high context windows pinned to gpu-11. It's a non-critical internal job. I'm killing the job: `kubectl -n batch delete job big-window-train-2026`

sam_w: job killed, reclaim visible across the pool. p95 latency back to normal, error rate down to baseline.

pagerduty: incident acknowledged by sam_w. Escalation to on-call lead (tara_ops) retained due to customer impact.

tara_ops: good work. Next steps: 1) keep route override until autoscale finishes expansion (approx 10m), 2) follow up with batch team to prevent future long-context on production pools, 3) create a post-incident ticket with logs and root-cause hypothesis.

marta_cs: customer outreach updated: "Mitigation applied; traffic rerouted and background jobs terminated. We expect full recovery. Will follow up with root-cause and compensations if needed."

sam_w: capturing diagnostics: nvml dump + model repo traces attached to PD incident PD-8472 (link). Stack trace: `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED at linalg/allocator.cu:412`

cheng_l: hypothesis: KV cache compaction didn't trigger aggressively under this specific workload distribution, causing memory fragmentation and unexpected OOMs on certain nodes. Will add an instrumentation flag to increase compaction aggressiveness for pool-g1 as an intermediate fix.

tara_ops: handoff notes for next oncall: pool-g1 had a transient KV cache fragmentation event causing OOMs on gpu-11. Mitigations performed: route override, IP rate-limit, drained gpu-11, killed offending batch job, and scaled pool by +2 nodes. Monitor for 1h, then revert route override if stable.

sam_w: leaving the channel, marking incident as resolved for now. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Incident PD-8472 status: resolved -> monitoring for 30m. Auto-close after 60m if no regressions.

marta_cs: filing follow-up ticket: RWD-INC-2026: "KV cache compaction tuning for pool-g1 to prevent OOMs under long-context bursts" assigned to eng-runtime (cheng_l) and infra (sam_w).

cheng_l: will open a small PR to enable more frequent compaction and add a saturation alarm to alert earlier before OOM.

sam_w: last checks: error rate 0.12% (baseline 0.08%), p95 latency +20ms above baseline for 5m window. Keeping monitoring on.

marta_cs: thanks everyone. I'll keep customers updated until follow-up ticket has RCA and plan.

(End of thread)
